from: UniProtKB release 2026_04: the 4,403 reviewed entries of the reference proteome UP000000625 of Escherichia coli strain K-12, one protein each; with the other forms that 11 of them describe, 4,415 sequences. The proteome holds 0 unreviewed entries: every protein of it is listed, for 4,403 genes.

shelves.label: Cell inner membrane
shelves.outside: In the periplasm, between the cell's two membranes
shelves.inside: Inside the cell: in the cytoplasm
shelves.note: Here stand also the 94 proteins whose entry says "Cell membrane" and not which: UniProt's vocabulary says that the cell membrane is known as the inner membrane where a cell has two. The lipid-anchored ones among them stand on the shelf of a membrane that is not named.

shelves.label: Cell outer membrane
shelves.inside: On the periplasmic face of the outer membrane
shelves.note: On its inside stand only proteins that an entry places at the outer membrane's periplasmic face. A protein free in the periplasm stands on the inner membrane's shelf, on its outside.

shelves.label: A membrane, not told which
shelves.outside: Beyond the inner membrane: in the periplasm, at the outer membrane or outside the cell
shelves.inside: On the cytoplasmic side of a membrane
shelves.note: Three kinds of protein. The 28 that an entry places in a membrane without naming it. The 40 lipid-anchored ones whose entry says "Cell membrane" with no experiment behind the statement (a rule of PROSITE or HAMAP: 19; a curator's inference: 18; no evidence given: 3): this file reads those words as not telling which membrane, since an entry that tells the membrane of a lipid-anchored protein names it, "Cell inner membrane" in 16 entries and "Cell outer membrane" in 38. And the 106 with no stated place whose entry carries a signal peptide: such a protein was carried across the inner membrane, and how far beyond it is not told.

between.rule: A protein free in the space between the two membranes (the periplasm, and the wall that lies in it) stands on the inner membrane's shelf, on its outside. A protein held at a membrane and facing that space stands on that membrane's shelf, on the side that faces the space: the outside of the inner shelf, the inside of the outer. A protein known only to lie beyond the inner membrane stands on the outside of the shelf of a membrane that is not named.

groups_from: A protein's Gene Ontology terms are those InterPro maps to any of its signatures and those UniProt gives its entry. With every broader term (by the ontology's kind-of and part-of links), the protein falls in the first district, in the order listed, one of whose terms it carries. A family's line stands in the district most of its classed members on that shelf fall in; of equal counts, the first listed. A protein that is the only member of its family stands in its own district. A part of no_family is a looser grouping: it stands in a district only if more than half of all its members on that shelf fall there. The choice of the districts' terms and their order is the viewer's, and is the planarian's and the human's.
family_from: A family is an InterPro entry of the type Family (InterPro 111.0). A protein is filed under the narrowest family among the InterPro entries UniProt gives it: one that is not a broader kind of another it carries, by InterPro's tree of entries. Where several unrelated families remain (670 proteins), it is the deepest in that tree, then the one fewest proteins of this catalogue are in, then the first by accession. This is the rule of the planarian's and the human's files, so a family has the same id in each.

family_notes.lines: A family has one line for each shelf that holds members of it, and one with a null shelf for its members that are on no shelf. A line is identified by id and shelf together; side, group, count, sides, file, at and units are of its members on that shelf alone.
family_notes.side: The side most of the line's members sit on; of equal counts, a membrane first.
family_notes.units: The inventory units for which a member on this line carries the family's signature: candidates by family alone.
family_notes.total: The family's members on every shelf and on none.
family_notes.counts: distinct_families is the number of families that have lines; families_in_all counts also the families of one, whose proteins are under 'lone'. In 'shelves' and 'no_shelf', 'families' is every family with a member there (its lines and its lone proteins), 'lines' the families' lines there, 'lone' the proteins that are the only member of their family, 'no_family' those with none.

no_family.label: No family assigned
no_family.parts_from: A protein with no family is filed under one part. If it carries an InterPro entry of the type Homologous superfamily, the part is that superfamily: a wider grouping than a family, by shared structure. Of several superfamilies it is the one fewest proteins of this catalogue carry, then the first by accession. The other two parts hold the proteins with only a domain, repeat or site signature, and those with no signature at all. A part has one line for each shelf, as a family has.

members_from.order: The table's lines are the members in order: every line of the families as listed here, then every part of 'lone', then every part of 'no_family'; within each, by gene name. A line's members are the next 'count' lines of the table. For a family's line and for a part of no_family, 'under' is its id and 'shelf' its shelf (empty for none); for a part of 'lone', 'under' is the protein's own family and 'family' that family's name.
members_from.files: A file holds the members of consecutive lines: a new file begins where the next line would take it past 2,000 members, so a line is never split. 'file' names the file and 'at' the first and one past the last of its members there. A member's shelf is its line's.
members_from.places: In the table a stated place is written with UniProt's identifiers, without their prefix: the place, then the topology and the face where the entry states them, joined by a full stop (0037.9909 is SL-0037 with SL-9909). 'place_words' gives the words of each.
members_from.step: python3 tools/build_ecoli_atlas.py members --out DIR writes the files from the two files.

side_notes.stated: The protein's reviewed UniProtKB entry states where it is, and the first place it states decides the shelf and the side: the cytoplasm, the periplasm or outside the cell; a membrane the protein is said to span; or a membrane with the face the protein is on. Where the first place names no side, a later statement of the same entry that names a part of that place decides. The mark 'evidence' says what stands behind the statement.
side_notes.predicted: Read from the entry's own features, where its words do not give the side. A membrane-spanning segment puts the protein in the membrane its entry states (4 proteins). A signal peptide with no such segment says that the protein was carried across the inner membrane: it stands on the outside of the inner membrane's shelf where the entry states that membrane (16 proteins), and on the outside of the shelf of a membrane that is not named where the entry does not tell the membrane (37) or states no place (106). UniProt's curators annotate these features from experiments, from likeness to other proteins and from prediction; its own pages name the predictors: TMHMM, Memsat, Phobius and a hydrophobic moment plot for the segments; Phobius, Predotar, SignalP and TargetP for the signal peptides. Each is named among the sources, with its terms and what rests on it. By the project's rule (the user, 15 November 2026), a value stands on the terms of the database it was read from, and the tool behind it is named and counted: the project's rule, not a legal opinion.
side_notes.none: The entry states a membrane or a place and not the side (the protein then stands apart beside that shelf, with the place in its mark 'where'), or it states no place of the cell and carries no membrane-spanning segment and no signal peptide (the protein is then on no shelf). Nothing is placed by guess.

placed_by.what: The place itself is on one side: the cytoplasm, the periplasm, or outside the cell.
The entry states that the protein spans the membrane (single-pass or multi-pass).
The entry states which face of the membrane the protein is on.
The entry states an anchor that holds a protein on the face away from the cytoplasm, and no face. No entry of this organism states one.
The first place names no side, and a later statement of the same entry names a part of that place and gives the side.
The entry states the membrane and not the side, and it carries a membrane-spanning segment: in the membrane.

The entry states the inner membrane, or a membrane it does not name, and not the side, and it carries a signal peptide and no membrane-spanning segment: beyond the inner membrane. Of a protein stated at the outer membrane a signal peptide settles nothing, since every such protein has crossed the inner membrane.
No place of the cell is stated, and the entry carries a membrane-spanning segment: in a membrane, not told which.
No place of the cell is stated, and the entry carries a signal peptide and no segment: beyond the inner membrane, and how far is not told.
The entry states the membrane or the place, and nothing in it settles the side.
No place of the cell is stated and nothing is predicted: on no shelf.

place_kinds.membrane: the shelf's membrane, or a part of it
place_kinds.whole: a compartment that one membrane bounds, or a structure at the membrane, with no part or face named
place_kinds.region: a region with more than one membrane, or none
place_kinds.elsewhere: not a place of the cell

place_notes: Every place the entries state, in UniProt's words, with the shelf and what the place names against its membrane (place_kinds), how the table's line was reached and which of the table's terms it rests on, and how many proteins it places as the statement that decided. One reading of this file goes beyond the table: a lipid-anchored protein whose entry says "Cell membrane", with no experiment behind the statement, stands on the shelf of a membrane that is not named (that shelf's note says why and how many).

isoforms.label: Forms described
isoforms.note: The canonical sequence and the other sequences its entry describes: in this organism, forms that start at another codon of the same gene. The marker stands for the canonical one.

seen.label: Evidence that the protein exists
seen.note: UniProt's level of evidence for the entry: at protein level, at transcript level, inferred from homology, predicted, or uncertain.

evidence.label: What stands behind the stated place
evidence.note: From UniProt's evidence codes on the statement: experiment: an experiment in a paper the entry cites; similarity: likeness to a protein of which it is known; curator: a curator's inference, or an author's statement that names no experiment; rule: a sequence model or a family rule, applied by a curator; not given: the entry gives no code, an older curated statement. Of several, the first in this order.

where.label: Stated place
where.note: The statement that decided the shelf, in UniProt's words: the place, then the topology and the face where the entry states them.

also.label: Also stated
also.note: The entry's other statements of place, in order and in UniProt's words.

family.label: Family, of which it is the only member here
family.note: The InterPro family's accession and name, for a protein listed among the only members of their families.

of.label: Stated for
of.note: The named form of the protein that the place is stated for, where the entry states none for the protein as a whole.

locus.label: Locus
locus.note: The gene's ordered locus name in the genome of strain K-12 substrain MG1655 (its b number), as UniProt gives it.

chemotaxis.label: Chemotaxis
chemotaxis.note: The entry carries UniProt's keyword 'Chemotaxis': the receptors, the proteins that pass their signal on, the motor's switch and stator, and the binding proteins that report sugars and peptides. 22 proteins: aer, cheA, cheB, cheR, cheW, cheY, cheZ, dppA, fliG, fliJ, fliL, fliM, fliN, fliO, mglB, motA, motB, rbsB, tap, tar, trg and tsr.

complex.label: Assembly it is part of
complex.note: By the Gene Ontology's cellular-component terms that UniProt gives the entry, with every narrower term: flagellum (bacterial-type flagellum, GO:0009288): 34; chemoreceptor array (methyl accepting chemotaxis protein complex, GO:0098561): 6; ribosome (ribosome, GO:0005840): 59; RNA polymerase (DNA-directed RNA polymerase complex, GO:0000428): 7; ATP synthase (proton-transporting ATP synthase complex, GO:0045259): 8. Of several, the first listed.

highlights.note: For the marks that pick out a machine (chemotaxis, and the assemblies of 'complex'): each protein that carries the mark, with the line it stands on, so that a page can light the markers that hold them without opening every family. 'kind' says whether 'under' is a family, a part of 'lone' or a part of 'no_family'; a null shelf is no shelf.
